text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm trying to standardize how our inference services bootstrap OpenTelemetry across Python/Go/Rust. We keep getting mismatched exporters and noisy kv-cache spans. Thoughts?

alex: Nice. Main pain: different defaults + libraries force people to opt-in, so some services end up untraced or with broken exporters. Also shutdown behavior differs per SDK.

sam: Agree. For inference, we must avoid span explosion: a single request can spawn 10k token-level spans if we don't coalesce. We should document a pattern: one top-level request span + optional 'kv-cache' condensed span with counts instead of per-token spans.

leah: From infra side: exporter routing matters — prefer agent fallback instead of requiring OTLP endpoint env var everywhere. Env precedence: explicit OTLP endpoint > OTEL_AGENT (local) > no-op. That keeps prod safe and local dev easy.

ryan: UX idea: add a tiny bootstrap helper in each SDK repo that applies our defaults. Example usage: `redwood_otel.init()` and it wires resource attrs, sampling, and exporter fallback. Keep it minimal so teams can override.

maya: Can we sketch minimal default behavior? I'm thinking: resource attrs: service.name, infra.instance_id, model.name, model.version, hw.tier. Sampling: parent_based(0.001) for production, 1.0 in dev. Exporter: OTLP_HTTP to env or fallback to local agent socket. Graceful shutdown flush timeout 2s.

alex: Sounds good. For Python (opentelemetry-sdk) snippet we can do:
```
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, ConsoleSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter

def init_redwood_otel(opts):
    tp = TracerProvider()
    exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=opts.get('OTLP_ENDPOINT')) if opts.get('OTLP_ENDPOINT') else ConsoleSpanExporter()
    tp.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
    trace.set_tracer_provider(tp)
```
Keep it tiny and documented.

sam: For Go we should wrap `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` setup in a single function `redwoodotel.Init(ctx, cfg)` that respects env priority and returns a Shutdown func. Very important to return a close func for graceful Rollout/kill.

leah: Rust teams want minimal deps. Offer a `redwood-otel` crate that pulls in `opentelemetry` and exposes builder with `with_agent_fallback()` so they don't need to reimplement logic.

ryan: Regarding spans: we should define canonical attributes for inference ops so dashboards can group them: `inference.model.name`, `inference.model.variant`, `inference.request.type` (chat/generate/embed), `inference.tokens.input`, `inference.tokens.output`, `inference.batch.size`. Encourage counts rather than sequences for token details.

maya: Agreed. Also propose a pattern for KV cache: emit a `cache.hit_summary` span at the end with `hits`, `misses`, `bytes_saved` instead of per-kv spans. That keeps traces compact and useful.

alex: Batching/exporter semantics: set `max_queue_size=2048`, `scheduled_delay_ms=200` as defaults (can be overridden). Add a hard cap on buffered bytes to avoid OOM under backpressure.

sam: Retention/ingest note: telemetry ingestion will keep traces for 7 days by default for infra teams; we should surface sampling tiers so product teams can request longer retention for eval traces.

leah: Operationally: telemetry-bot can monitor if services are no-oping the exporter (missing OTEL config) and post a weekly report to #eng-platform. We should add an opt-out tag for experimental services.

telemetry-bot: Actionable: detected 8 services in staging without exporter configured. Suggestion: add redwood_otel.init(); see internal doc: https://go.redwood/otel-bootstrap (placeholder). :warning:

ryan: One more subtlety — context propagation across worker pools. For Rust/Golang we must ensure ctx is passed through task queues; for Python we need to use contextvars properly in async loops. We'll add examples per lang in repo.

maya: Ok next steps: 1) I'll draft the minimal API surface for `redwood_otel.init()` with env precedence and defaults. 2) Alex/Sam/Leah will make short PRs in each sdk repo with the helper + README examples. 3) telemetry-bot config PR to enable weekly exporter-health check.

alex: I'll add shutdown hook tests to the Go helper — verify exporter flush within 2s on SIGTERM.

sam: I'll do the Python unit/integration that simulates high token throughput and ensure spans stay compact.

leah: I'll prototype agent fallback in staging and report performance/latency impact.

maya: Thanks — if anyone hits a blocker ping me. Also callout for SRE: if we change defaults we should run a canary to ensure sampling rate change doesn't flood ingest.

ryan: Noted. I'll schedule a 30-min sync after the initial PRs land. :calendar:
